paragraphs: This checklist is for self-questioning only, not hiring criteria, ability scores, or product and production safety conclusions. The page follows US O*NET-SOC 51-3093.00 Food Cooking Machine Operators and Tenders (the fixed Chinese index name is Food Machine Operators and Tenders; main work operates or tends steam vats, fryers, pressure cookers, kettles, and boilers to make food).

Paper exercise | Use the fictional F01 ingredient plan, batch log, and test records below to calculate ingredient differences, output allocation, and recorded times, then draft unresolved issues and handover. Use given data only, without starting equipment, adjusting temperature or pressure, producing or tasting products. Check reference deliverables and record omissions.

Fit signals | O*NET highlights considerable task/priority freedom (75%), controlled indoor work daily (75%), considerable decision freedom (75%), teamwork extremely important (71%), constant contact (71%), continual or almost continual walking/running (63%) and standing (60%), daily face-to-face discussions (74%), daily decisions (50%). If you willingly work beside cooking equipment adjusting by recipes and processes, notice readings and product conditions, and accept heat and steam, daily demands are closer to your style.

Caution signals | Work near heat and steam, continual or almost continual standing (60%) and walking (63%). Accuracy is very important (47%); some do not report daily protection (15% never), reflecting varied workshop protection and exposure. Error consequences serious (29%); typical weeks over 40 hours (37%). If standing and heat are difficult or vigilance toward temperature/pressure errors and batch scrap is insufficient, weigh these costs.

Preparation | Complete F01 records first, then check target equipment, shifts, training, and authority. Paper work observes recording habits only, not cooking/sterilization, heat adaptation, independent operation, or release competence.

Safe sample (fictional): Given cooked-product order (recipe and feed specifications, temperature/pressure/time targets, consistency or acidity), draft within 60 minutes: order/recipe checks, setup/start plan (temperature/pressure/time/stirring), monitoring (gauges/steam/flow/product), samples/tests (color/consistency/viscosity/acidity/gravity), abnormality and stop/report workflow. Specify mandatory escalation for uncontrolled parameters, alarms, ingredient/recipe deviations, abnormal tests.

Scope | O*NET-SOC 51-3093.00 food cooking equipment. Jobs may also mix, grind, feed, and sample; adjacent steps are not absolutely excluded. Recipe development, repair, final release require role/authority checks.

entries: Orders/recipes | Time, temperature, feed specifications | Check ingredients, feed, cooking requirements, batch identifiers and status.
Setup/start | Temperature, pressure, time | Set controls, start conveyors/machines/pumps, prepare steam/oil/compressed air.
Feed/stir | Valves/conveyors | Feed prescribed amounts manually or by lifting, operate valves/pumps to add/discharge, start stirrers/paddles.
Monitor/adjust | Gauges/products | Observe gauges/scales/product, adjust temperature, pressure, flow for specified conditions.
Samples/quality | Color, consistency, viscosity, acidity, gravity | Sample during processing and test quality, color, content and indicators, judge doneness.
Discharge/clean/handover | Records/hygiene | Remove, transfer or cool cooked products, clean/disinfect, record steps/batches and hand over.
